hub.meta: Compare Zapier, Make, n8n, Workato, Tray.io, LangChain, Pipedream, and Paperclip. Speed, self-hosting, AI agents, or enterprise governance: each of these platforms bets on a different one.
lead: Workflow automation is the unglamorous layer that decides whether your stack behaves like a system or a pile of browser tabs. These tools connect everything else: your CRM talks to your ESP, your forms feed your analytics, and your AI agents get somewhere to actually execute instead of drafting suggestions nobody reads.

The category splits two ways. Visual builders like Zapier and Make get you to a working run fast, but you rent the engine. Code-friendly platforms like n8n and LangChain hand you raw primitives and expect you to know what you're doing. Workato and Tray.io sit in the enterprise tier, wrapping both ideas in governance and a bigger invoice.

When you're comparing these in 2026, skip the "which one connects the most apps" table. They all connect enough apps. What separates them is whether a run can hold state across a long job, recover from failures without losing progress, and give an AI agent real operations to call. That last part matters more than the node count, and most comparison pages ignore it.
